templates.name: PostgreSQL
templates.compose:

    image: postgres:16
    environment:

      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}

notes: Reachable on the host port you set. Leave it internal by removing the port mapping if only other containers need it.

templates.name: Ghost
templates.tagline: Publishing platform for blogs and newsletters
templates.compose:
services:
  db:
    image: mysql:8
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: ghost
      MYSQL_USER: ghost
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "localhost", "-p${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 20
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/mysql
    restart: unless-stopped
  ghost:
    image: ghost:5
    environment:
      url: http://localhost:${PORT}
      database__client: mysql
      database__connection__host: db
      database__connection__user: ghost
      database__connection__password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      database__connection__database: ghost
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "${PORT}:2368"
    volumes:
      - content:/var/lib/ghost/content
    restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
  db:
  content:
notes: Set your real URL after first run so links and images resolve correctly.

templates.name: Media automation
templates.tagline: Jellyfin + Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr + Prowlarr + qBittorrent (VPN) + SABnzbd + Jellyseerr
templates.compose:
services:
  gluetun:
    image: qmcgaw/gluetun:v3
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    devices:
      - /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun
    environment:
      VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER: ${VPN_PROVIDER}
      VPN_TYPE: openvpn
      OPENVPN_USER: ${OPENVPN_USER}
      OPENVPN_PASSWORD: ${OPENVPN_PASSWORD}
      SERVER_COUNTRIES: ${VPN_COUNTRIES}
      FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS: 172.28.0.0/16
      TZ: ${TZ}
    ports:
      - "${QBIT_PORT}:8080"
    volumes:
      - gluetun:/gluetun
    networks:
      - media
    restart: unless-stopped

templates.name: Observability
templates.tagline: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and host/container metrics — a monitoring stack wired to graph on first open.
templates.compose:
configs:
  prometheus_yml:
    content: |
      global:
        scrape_interval: ${SCRAPE_INTERVAL:-15s}
      alerting:
        alertmanagers:
          - static_configs: [{ targets: ['alertmanager:9093'] }]
      scrape_configs:
        - job_name: prometheus
          static_configs: [{ targets: ['localhost:9090'] }]
        - job_name: node
          static_configs: [{ targets: ['node-exporter:9100'] }]
        - job_name: cadvisor
          static_configs: [{ targets: ['cadvisor:8080'] }]
        - job_name: alertmanager
          static_configs: [{ targets: ['alertmanager:9093'] }]
  alertmanager_yml:
    content: |
      route:
        receiver: 'null'
      receivers:
        - name: 'null'
  grafana_ds:
    content: |
      apiVersion: 1
      datasources:
        - name: Prometheus
          type: prometheus
          access: proxy
          url: http://prometheus:9090
          isDefault: true
services:
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=${PROM_RETENTION:-15d}'
    configs:
      - source: prometheus_yml
        target: /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:${PROM_PORT:-9090}:9090']
    volumes: [prometheus_data:/prometheus]
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.0
    configs:
      - source: alertmanager_yml
        target: /etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:${ALERT_PORT:-9093}:9093']
    volumes: [alertmanager_data:/alertmanager]
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
  node-exporter:
    image: prom/node-exporter:v1.8.2
    command:
      - '--path.procfs=/host/proc'
      - '--path.sysfs=/host/sys'
      - '--path.rootfs=/rootfs'
      - '--collector.filesystem.mount-points-exclude=^/(sys|proc|dev|host|etc)($$|/)'
    volumes:
      - /proc:/host/proc:ro
      - /sys:/host/sys:ro
      - /:/rootfs:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
  cadvisor:
    image: gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor:v0.49.1
    privileged: true
    devices: ['/dev/kmsg']
    volumes:
      - /:/rootfs:ro
      - /var/run:/var/run:ro
      - /sys:/sys:ro
      - /var/lib/docker/:/var/lib/docker:ro
      - /dev/disk/:/dev/disk:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    environment:
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER: ${GRAFANA_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP: "false"
    configs:
      - source: grafana_ds
        target: /etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources/prometheus.yml
    ports: ['${GRAFANA_PORT:-3000}:3000']
    volumes: [grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana]
    depends_on: [prometheus]
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
networks: { monitoring: {} }
volumes: { prometheus_data: {}, alertmanager_data: {}, grafana_data: {} }

notes: Grafana is the dashboard (password-gated). Prometheus and Alertmanager have no built-in auth, so they bind to localhost on the host and are reached through meshDeck's forwarding — not a public port.

cAdvisor runs privileged with read-only host root, disk and Docker access; node-exporter reads the whole host filesystem read-only. That is host-level visibility — deploy only on a host you trust meshDeck with.

The Grafana admin password is set on first launch and kept in your vault. If you change it inside Grafana, update it in meshDeck too: a redeploy will not reset it while the Grafana data volume persists.
Grafana opens with the Prometheus datasource already wired. Import a dashboard to start graphing — e.g. Grafana.com ID 1860 (node-exporter) and 14282 (cAdvisor).

variables.help: The Ollama API, bound to localhost — reached in-app, never on the LAN.

notes: No model is included. After it's up, open Open WebUI and pull one — e.g. llama3.2, qwen2.5 or phi3 — from the model menu.

The first person to sign up to Open WebUI becomes the admin, with full control (an admin can run code in the container and drive the model). Sign up immediately, then turn off new sign-ups (Admin → Settings). It's safest reached in-app over meshDeck rather than a public port.
Ollama's API has no authentication, so it's bound to localhost only and reached in-app — never put it on your LAN.
Models are large: a 7B model is about 4–5 GB, and they share the host's main disk, so pulling several can fill it. Remove models you don't use (in Open WebUI, or 'ollama rm').
It runs on CPU by default, so it works on any host (just slower). A 7B model wants roughly 8 GB of free RAM. For an NVIDIA GPU, add a device reservation and the NVIDIA container toolkit.
First launch downloads a small embedding model for search — give it a minute on first boot.
